text: Huh, there's something weird by its nostril. Wait, what is that?
Turns out that's not just a crack - it's a dedicated exit, just for breathing out.
When it exhales, the air slips out sideways through that slit - so the fresh scent coming in up front stays undisturbed.
So unlike us, a dog never actually stops smelling - not even while breathing out.
Thanks to that, dogs can take quick little sniffs, one after another, without ever losing track of a scent.
Scientists have actually caught that exhaled air escaping sideways on camera, using special imaging techniques.
And they say a dog's nose stays wet to trap even more scent particles.
